items.headline: Microsoft 365 and Outlook outage traced to latent July gateway bug; Nadella calls it a 'perfect storm'
items.summary: Microsoft says a bug from a July gateway update, triggered by Teams failover traffic and reduced capacity, left over 80% of Exchange Online gateway servers unresponsive for almost 24 hours from 12 November. Nadella said Microsoft should have tested earlier.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Microsoft preliminary report and CEO comments, relayed by outlets; report itself not read. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 16:20 GMT, 12 November 2026 (outage start per Microsoft report, via BleepingComputer)

sections.happened: Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams and Copilot, were disrupted worldwide from 11:20 ET (16:20 UK) on 12 November. Microsoft said customer impact ended at 11:10 ET (16:10 UK) on 13 November. Teams, OneDrive and SharePoint recovered earlier; Exchange Online did not. Executive Vice President Charles Lamanna apologised. On 18 November Satya Nadella told CNBC it was a 'perfect storm' and that Microsoft should have tested earlier and built isolation so there was no global outage.
sections.technical: Per Microsoft's preliminary post-incident report: a defect from a July update to Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers made servers unresponsive under certain load. It had run for over three months unnoticed. Triggers: Teams failover to Exchange Online infrastructure about 15 hours earlier, plus roughly 14% of gateway capacity already offline. Redirected traffic overwhelmed other servers; over 80% were unresponsive within two hours. Lab load tests used weaker, fewer-core hardware. Restarts re-triggered overload.
sections.guidance: Microsoft said it has increased capacity, improved monitoring and added safeguards against traffic redirection triggering cascading failures. A final post-incident report was expected later in the week of 16 November.
sections.differing: Officials and commentators speculated about cyberattacks or AI. Microsoft says malicious activity and AI agents were not the cause (per Scientific American). Nadella separately linked faster AI-driven patching to instability; this is his view, not part of the report.
sections.unknown: The final post-incident report is awaited. The relation to Microsoft's separate Teams outage that day is unclear. Number of affected customers is unpublished.

sources.title: BleepingComputer: Microsoft says months-old bug caused global Microsoft 365 outage
CNBC: Microsoft put the AI threat to software behind it. Then came the outage

items.headline: France blames Iran for supermarket fridge cyberattack
items.summary: France's foreign minister called an October cyberattack on connected supermarket freezers unprecedented in scale. Reported US intelligence links it to Iran with low confidence; the attribution is unconfirmed.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Attribution rests on anonymous US officials and press reports; French CERT report not read.
items.firstReported: 18 November 2026, Schneier on Security (citing reporting on US officials)

sections.happened: Attackers reportedly remotely forced defrost cycles on connected supermarket freezers at about 700 French retailers in October, spoiling produce and starting fires in some units. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot called it an attack of unprecedented scale. US agencies reportedly assess Iran as responsible with low confidence.
sections.differing: Schneier's US-official reporting says the assessment links the attacks to Iran generally, not a specific group. Commenters cite a French CERT report claiming Farsi code traces; this was not read.
sections.unknown: No French government attribution text read. Vendor, technique and CVEs not confirmed. Similar European attacks are under investigation.

items.headline: EU Commission confirms AI-assisted cyberattack that disrupted systems
items.summary: The European Commission confirmed a cyber campaign using publicly available AI tools, detected 22 October. HR, medical reimbursement and translation systems were taken offline. It says it has found no evidence of a staff data breach; the investigation continues.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Commission spokesperson confirmed attack and AI tool use at 19 November briefing.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026, Politico Brussels Playbook (morning); Commission confirmation at midday briefing, per Infosecurity Magazine

sections.happened: Politico reported on 19 November that a cyberattack had disrupted internal Commission systems for over ten days. Spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed a detected cyber campaign, said the intrusion was detected on 22 October and confirmed as an attack on 26 October, and said several applications were taken down as a precaution, most since restored. Affected systems reportedly included Sysper (HR), MyPMO (medical reimbursement) and translation services; Sysper failed again on 18 November. Salaries were reportedly paid on time.
sections.technical: Regnier said the attack used publicly available AI tools. Politico's sources, as relayed by The Register, named ARTEX, an open-source LLM-driven penetration-testing framework. CERT-EU's 5 November note lists T1595, T1588.002 and T1190 for ARTEX use. ARTEX has no built-in model; operators supply one. Its author withdrew the repository in October, and forks remain. The entry route into the Commission has not been disclosed. The FBI reported over 1,600 exposed ARTEX consoles.
sections.guidance: CERT-EU's ARTEX note advises limiting internet exposure, isolating management panels, emergency-patching exposed assets, enabling MFA, monitoring privileged accounts, using EDR and a WAF, and hunting for ARTEX-consistent scanning patterns.
sections.differing: Politico's sources point to ARTEX; Regnier confirmed AI tools but, per Infosecurity Magazine, gave no tool name. Staff reports of JSIS and translation outages are not covered in the Commission's statement.
sections.unknown: Attacker identity, initial access method, systems affected in full, and whether any staff data was accessed remain undisclosed; the investigation is ongoing.

sources.title: CERT-EU: From Penetration Testing to Cyber Threat: Beware of ARTEX
Infosecurity Magazine: European Commission Confirms AI-Driven Cyber-Attack Took Systems Offline
The Register: European Commission scrambles to contain AI-assisted cyberattack

items.headline: Russian state-linked actor turns cloud breach into further access
items.summary: Google GTIG says Russia-nexus espionage group COLD RELIC used data from one US cloud breach to impersonate staff and compromise a second US organisation through federated SSO.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Google GTIG and Mandiant report; victims unnamed; no independent corroboration found. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026, Dark Reading (GTIG blog date not captured)

sections.happened: Google GTIG reported COLD RELIC intrusions at two US organisations: late 2025 via a stolen super admin account, and in 2026 via phishing impersonating a first-victim employee. Stolen data enabled the impersonation. Victims are not named. GTIG says the group remains active, with phishing seen in November 2026.
sections.technical: Residential proxy logins; MFA push fatigue until approval; rogue passkeys and MFA devices; domain-wide Google Workspace Takeout export; Alert Center notifications deleted; Entra ID token theft via federated SSO. ATT&CK IDs not in sources read.
sections.guidance: GTIG advises phishing-resistant MFA, restricting and auditing passkey registrations, hardening MFA registration, auditing OAuth grants, and verifying unexpected messages through a separate channel.
sections.differing: No opposing accounts found; coverage by Dark Reading and Help Net Security relays the same GTIG findings.
sections.unknown: Names of the two organisations and what the second victim lost; whether other victims exist; exact intrusion dates beyond 'earlier this year'.

sources.title: Google Cloud Threat Intelligence (GTIG): COLD RELIC: A Case Study in Impersonation and Compromise

items.firstReported: 16 Nov 2026 service-disruption notice (later found to be a security incident); disclosed 19 Nov 2026, The Hacker News

sections.happened: N-able began investigating a Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud disruption on 16 Nov 2026, first attributed to configuration. It later found unauthorised access to one server. Management UI, APIs, quarantine and logging remain offline; mail flow and filtering continue. Restoration was ongoing as of 8 a.m. UTC, 19 Nov.
sections.technical: Initial access method, threat actor and malware not disclosed. Affected services: Mail Assure and SpamExperts in Americas, APAC and Europe regions. N-able says the incident is unrelated to the N-central vulnerabilities (Able2Shell).
sections.guidance: N-able says it has contacted partners about whether action is required for their environment; customers should contact N-able Technical Support.
sections.unknown: Attacker identity, access route and full scope; N-able has not closed its investigation on customer mailbox data.

items.headline: Rakuten Securities breach could affect 15 million customers
items.summary: Japanese brokerage Rakuten Securities says test-environment data leaked on 11 Nov 2026; about 4.47 million accounts had personal and asset fields exposed, and 11.25 million had branch codes and login IDs taken.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Company apology and disclosure, 17 Nov 2026; investigation ongoing; reported by Infosecurity Magazine. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 company apology (Japan date), per Infosecurity Magazine; Japan Times 18 Nov 2026

sections.happened: Rakuten Securities said unauthorised access was discovered on 16 Nov 2026 and that information in a test environment may have leaked to an external party on 11 Nov. About 4.47 million accounts had fields including name, date of birth, address, employer, withdrawal account and asset data exposed. Passwords and PINs are said not taken; investigation continues.
sections.technical: Root cause not yet published. Production customer data was present in a test environment system. The company said there is no sign of unauthorised access to customer accounts. Over 90% of customers log in with FIDO2 passkeys.
sections.guidance: Rakuten Securities warned customers of follow-on phishing and urged those not yet using passkeys to switch, to reduce account takeover risk.
sections.differing: Infosecurity says 'nearly 16 million' people; the two account groups total about 15.7 million, and the headline says 15 million.
sections.unknown: Root cause and recipient of the data; how the test environment was exposed; whether data has been sold or published.

items.headline: Wellington IT breach exposes saved payee data at around 40 Irish credit unions
items.summary: An attack on Wellington IT, a credit union banking software supplier, exposed saved payee details at about 40 Irish credit unions. Login credentials and funds reportedly unaffected.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Affected credit unions, Wellington IT and a minister acknowledge; scope under investigation. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: Tue 17 Nov 2026 first reports (Irish outlets); The Register 19 Nov 11:45 UTC

sections.happened: Affected credit unions say attackers exploited a flaw in Wellington IT's online banking platform between 2 and 4 Oct; it was closed 6 Oct. Credit unions were told only in recent days. Minister Robert Troy called the delay 'not acceptable'.
sections.technical: Attacker retrieved saved payee records linked to members. Exposed fields include payee names and nicknames, BICs, IBANs, sort codes, payment references and payee addresses. Vulnerability details beyond the flaw's exploitation window are not published.
sections.guidance: St Canice's warns members not to transfer money on anyone's claim that it must be moved for safety, and not to share PINs or access codes.
sections.differing: Clare Echo reports 'malicious requests' recorded 6 Oct; The Register says exploitation was 2 to 4 Oct. Irish Independent reports possibly hundreds of thousands of members; no official count.
sections.unknown: Which individual records were retrieved, the full list of affected members, and how access was gained. Wellington IT is investigating with outside experts; no primary Wellington statement was retrieved.

items.headline: TfL takes Oyster photocard site offline after compromise of about 265,000 customer accounts
items.summary: Transport for London says around 265,000 Oyster photocard customers may have had account details compromised after unauthorised emails were sent from its systems on 16 November. The site is offline; the ICO is notified; the intrusion method is undisclosed.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: TfL's director of technology statements, reported by The Register, Infosecurity and Telegraph. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026, 22:26 UK (Telegraph, via Yahoo News)

sections.happened: TfL says it became aware on 16 November, when Oyster photocard customers received emails, sent from TfL's own systems, asking them to create accounts they already held. It took the photocard website offline and later said about 265,000 customers' account details may have been compromised. Affected card types include Zip Oyster, Student, Care Leaver, 60+ London, Apprentice and Veterans photocards. TfL says the incident is contained, the ICO has been told, and there is no evidence yet of misuse. Existing photocards still work at barriers; renewals and journey-history queries go through customer services. No restoration date has been given.
sections.technical: TfL has not disclosed the access vector, the actor, or the exact fields taken. Its assessment is that passwords, bank or payment card details, journey data, and names and dates of birth of Zip Oyster children were not accessed. The unauthorised emails came from TfL's own systems as a result of the compromise. No CVE, malware or IOCs have been published.
sections.guidance: TfL says it will ask all photocard customers to change their password, security question and answer, and advises changing the password on any other service where it was reused. Customers needing renewals or journey history should contact TfL Customer Services.
sections.differing: The Telegraph reports names, contact details and dates of birth may have been accessed. The Register and Infosecurity report TfL's list of what was not compromised and do not list the fields taken. TfL's statement is the better-supported source.
sections.unknown: Entry method, attacker identity, exact data fields, when the site returns, and any link to TfL's 2024 breach; The Register says nothing suggests one.

items.summary: Ransomware gang n0n leaked a dataset tied to Visa's Asia-Pacific premium dining and loyalty programmes. Visa says a third-party provider was involved and no card or payment data was affected.

items.labelBasis: Visa acknowledged an incident; the leak and record counts come from the group and Cybernews. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026 (time not stated); Cybernews

sections.happened: Visa confirmed it was aware of claims and said an incident at a third-party service provider in Asia-Pacific was involved, not Visa systems. Ransomware gang n0n posted a stolen dataset after extortion talks reportedly failed. Cybernews counted over 6,000 premium customers in the data.

items.headline: Gentlemen ransomware claims Nvidia breach; Nvidia cites possible third-party incident
items.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware group listed Nvidia on its leak site with a roughly 10-day countdown but no evidence. Nvidia says it is investigating an incident that may have affected a third-party partner and has found no sign its own systems were affected.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Group listing without samples; Nvidia reports no indication of its own systems affected.
items.firstReported: 18-19 November 2026; leak-site listing dated 18 November (Cybernews, SecurityWeek, iThome)

sections.happened: The Gentlemen ransomware group added Nvidia to its dark-web leak site on 18 November 2026. The listing has a short company description, a Tox contact ID and a countdown (234 hours, under 10 days per Cybernews). Nvidia told SecurityWeek it is investigating an incident that may have affected a third-party partner, found no indication its systems or networks were affected, and continues to monitor.
sections.technical: The listing gives no data types, samples, business unit or intrusion date. The Gentlemen is a ransomware-as-a-service operation active since about mid-2025, using double extortion; Microsoft tracks operators as Storm-2697. Sophos reports affiliates use compromised credentials and legitimate administrative tools. Cybernews cites the tracker Ransomware.live at 1,123 claimed victims. No CVEs or IOCs published for this claim.
sections.differing: The group implies it holds Nvidia-related data. Nvidia points to a third-party partner and no impact on its own systems. Cybernews' researcher says the group has previously exaggerated claims, misattributed victims and reused data; the partner is unnamed.
sections.unknown: Which partner is involved, whether any data was stolen, what it contains, and whether the group will publish after the countdown.

items.headline: Credential stealer in Microsoft agent-framework Python package
items.summary: Two malicious releases of Microsoft's agent-framework on PyPI, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, ran a credential stealer on every Python start. PyPI quarantined both; 1.26.0 is the last clean version.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Multiple security firms' analyses; PyPI quarantine reported; Microsoft has not commented publicly. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026, 20:35 UTC (1.26.1 upload, per Aikido); first press report CSO Online, 18 Nov 2026

sections.happened: On 17 Nov 2026 versions 1.26.1 (20:35 UTC) and 1.26.2 (21:08 UTC) of agent-framework appeared on PyPI carrying a stealer. The package has about 192,534 monthly downloads (OX). PyPI quarantined both; the attacker uploaded 1.26.2 after 1.26.1 was quarantined. Microsoft had not publicly explained how publishing access was obtained.
sections.technical: Payload in agent_framework_meta.pth runs on every Python start without import. Harvests environment secrets, cloud and CI tokens, Azure managed-identity and DevOps OIDC tokens from up to 300 processes. Exfiltrates zlib/base64 JSON to webhook.site.
sections.guidance: Pin agent-framework to 1.26.0; treat secrets reachable from affected hosts as compromised and rotate them; review OIDC permissions, federated credentials and managed-identity role assignments (StepSecurity, OX).
sections.differing: OX says the stealer requested new tokens; StepSecurity stresses there is no confirmation that any tokens were issued.
sections.unknown: How the attacker obtained publishing rights; whether any tokens were issued; how many hosts ran either version.

items.headline: Apache Roller CVE-2026-129448: unauthenticated RCE under active exploitation
items.summary: Apache confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 9.8), an unauthenticated XML-RPC deserialization RCE in Roller 4.0.0 to 6.1.4. Fixed in 6.1.6; attack details not published.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Apache Software Foundation advisory states active exploitation; no attack details given. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 (Apache advisory, per The Hacker News and BleepingComputer, 18 Nov); UK time not stated

sections.happened: The Apache Software Foundation advisory of 17 Nov says CVE-2026-129448 is being actively exploited. It is the same flaw as CVE-2026-82384, patched in September 2026, which listed only Roller 6.1.5. Attackers, targets and victim counts are undisclosed.
sections.technical: Unsafe deserialization in the XML-RPC endpoint: vendor extension types are deserialized before the requester is authenticated, giving unauthenticated RCE. CVSS 9.8. Affected 4.0.0 through 6.1.4; fixed in 6.1.6. Credited to researcher n0mi1k.
sections.guidance: Apache: upgrade to 6.1.6 or later. Interim: set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml or remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc mapping; restart. Admin UI toggle is not enough.
sections.differing: SecurityWeek notes the earlier advisory listed only 6.1.5 as affected; the expanded 4.0.0 to 6.1.4 range is Apache's. Outlets disagree on whether Apache named any targets; none did.
sections.unknown: Exploitation method, threat actors, number of compromised servers and targets are not disclosed by Apache. The primary advisory itself was not retrieved.

items.headline: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938): memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK Base64 decoder; exploitation attempts reported
items.summary: Calif disclosed CVE-2026-114938, a heap-corruption flaw in OpenJDK on AVX-512 VBMI x86-64 CPUs. Fixes shipped 17 Nov. GreyNoise and WatchTowr report probing; no confirmed intrusions.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Oracle, OpenJDK, CISA and vendors acknowledge the flaw; probing is sensor-reported only.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026, about 21:00 UK time (1pm PT), Calif write-up at calif.io; Oracle and OpenJDK patched the same day

sections.happened: Calif disclosed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) on 17 Nov, a memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder. Oracle and OpenJDK released fixes the same day. CISA issued an emergency advisory. Calif reports unauthenticated RCE against default Jira, Confluence, Jenkins and Keycloak.
sections.technical: Malformed Base64 (64 'A' characters plus '=') yields a negative output length, causing a 64-byte write into a 50-byte buffer. Oracle scores CVSS 3.1 8.1; Calif scores CVSS 4.0 9.2. Affects OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later, 21, 25 and 27 on x86-64 with AVX-512 VBMI. ARM not affected.
sections.guidance: Per Tenable, fixed Oracle and Temurin builds are 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 and 27.0.1.1. Per Calif, interim JVM flag -XX:UseAVX=2 disables AVX-512 on x86-64 hosts.
sections.differing: Infosecurity says no in-the-wild exploitation as of 18 Nov; SecurityWeek reports GreyNoise and WatchTowr probing by 19 Nov, with no confirmed intrusions. OX Security estimates under 0.12% of JVMs at RCE risk.
sections.unknown: Whether probing becomes successful exploitation, and which vendor builds and cloud services are patched. Calif withholds per-application exploits; VulnCheck sells a full RCE exploit to customers.

items.headline: NGINX critical flaws (nginx2root) with public PoC; F5 patches issued
items.summary: F5 patched five critical NGINX flaws on 18 November, led by CVE-2026-123007, an HTTP/2 heap overflow present since 1.9.5. Public proof-of-concept code exists; no exploitation in the wild is reported. Root on the host needs a separate Linux kernel bug.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: F5 advisory and CERT-EU confirm; independent researchers demonstrated exploitation.
items.firstReported: 18 November 2026, F5 advisory K000163926 (CERT-EU advisory same day, 17:30)

sections.happened: On 18 November 2026 F5 released NGINX Open Source 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 and NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1, fixing five flaws grouped as nginx2root: CVE-2026-123007, -123633, -123634, -121810 and -113425, each CVSS 4.0 9.2. Xint, Wiz, Rapid7 and others reported them. Rapid7 and Censys published PoC code. Censys estimates about 9 million services run affected versions with HTTP/2 on. No exploitation in the wild reported; CVE-2026-123007 was not in CISA KEV.
sections.technical: CVE-2026-123007 is an integer overflow in HTTP/2 flow control causing a heap out-of-bounds write, present since 1.9.5 (2015). It needs only HTTP/2 enabled. Code runs as the worker user; F5 says execution needs ASLR disabled or bypassed, which Wiz and Rapid7 report achieving. Rapid7's exploit needs about 128 GB of HTTP/2 traffic. Xint chained it with a Linux SCTP kernel bug to reach root, including from Docker. Others: -123633 HTTP/2 use-after-free, -121810 HTTP/3, -123634 resolver, -113425 mail proxy.
sections.guidance: F5 and CERT-EU advise upgrading, prioritising internet-facing systems. CIRCL lists disabling HTTP/2 as a temporary mitigation, which does not cover the other three flaws. Fully restart NGINX after upgrading; a reload leaves the old binary running. NGINX Plus R34–R36 had no fix listed.
sections.differing: Severity: F5 gives CVSS 4.0 9.2; CERT-EU and Next cite CVSS 3.1 8.1. Distribution status conflicts: The Hacker News said Ubuntu had no fix; Next reported Ubuntu, Alpine and Amazon Linux fixed.
sections.unknown: Whether attackers are exploiting it. Fix timing for NGINX Plus R34–R36 and for Debian and Red Hat stable releases is unclear. Real-world exploitability at scale is unmeasured.

items.headline: PHP security releases fix 18 CVEs, including critical PHP-FPM request smuggling RCE
items.summary: PHP released fixes on 19 Nov for all supported branches (8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36), fixing 18 CVEs including CVE-2026-129289 (CVSS 9.2), a PHP-FPM request smuggling RCE in specific proxy setups.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: PHP security team issued advisory and releases; details from Aikido and press reports. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (Wednesday PHP advisory, per The Register); releases 19 Nov; UK time not stated

sections.happened: The PHP security team warned on 18 Nov that critical fixes would cover all supported versions. Releases on 19 Nov (PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36) fix 18 CVEs, per Aikido. CVE-2026-115560 was flagged in an informational advisory on 23 Oct.
sections.technical: CVE-2026-129289: PHP-FPM request smuggling, CVSS 9.2, unauthenticated PHP code execution where nginx, Apache, HAProxy or LSAPI reuse backend connections. CVE-2026-115560 needs session.serialize_handler and ini_set() switching to php.
sections.guidance: Aikido advises turning off backend connection reuse, keeping PHP-FPM and LSAPI listeners off untrusted networks, and setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until upgraded.
sections.differing: The Register says the critical issues need non-default or uncommon setups and, unlike PHP2Shell, were not leaked early. Aikido says the session mitigation does not cover the other critical issues.
sections.unknown: Exploitation status of the November fixes is not reported. The PHP advisory itself was not retrieved; CVSS and scope of the other 16 CVEs are not verified.

items.headline: Ukrainian strikes damage Crimean Bridge; Putin vows 'much more painful' response
items.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Strait bridge on 16–19 November, damaging the road span and railway; Putin said Russia will not negotiate and will retaliate, while promising repairs. Rail traffic resumed on 19 November. No injuries reported.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Putin acknowledged damage; Ukrainian officials and independent outlets report the strikes. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 16 Nov 2026 (attack began); Putin's first comment 19 Nov 2026, The Moscow Times/Reuters

sections.happened: Ukrainian forces attacked the 19-km Kerch Strait bridge repeatedly from 16 November, the Moscow Times says for the third time in four days. Meduza reports a missile and drone barrage on 17 November destroyed one road span and dropped an arch into the shipping channel. Ukraine's General Staff said Neptune missiles damaged railway tracks on 19 November; Russia suspended trains, which reopened by afternoon. At APEC in Shenzhen Putin acknowledged "serious damage" to the road section, promised rebuilding, and said Russia would not negotiate an energy truce.
sections.differing: Putin says the bridge is used exclusively for civilian purposes and that military cargo and fuel stopped crossing long ago. Ukraine treats it as a target; Zelensky called the strikes retaliation for Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure. Neither claim was independently verified in the sources read.
sections.unknown: Extent of damage to the railway section, repair timescale, the form of Russian retaliation, and the weapons used on each night are not independently established.

items.headline: Suspected Houthi missile hits PIF Tower in Riyadh's financial district
items.summary: A suspected Houthi missile struck PIF Tower, Saudi wealth fund headquarters in Riyadh, on 19 November, the second hit on a KAFD landmark in under two weeks. Reuters reported no immediate casualties; the Houthis had not claimed this strike.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Coalition acknowledged missile threat and damage; Reuters, AFP and Semafor corroborate. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: Morning of 19 Nov 2026 (UK time not stated); Reuters via Al-Monitor

sections.happened: Reuters reported that PIF Tower, Riyadh's tallest building and headquarters of the Public Investment Fund, was struck early on Thursday 19 November by a suspected Houthi missile. Windows were blown out across seven to eight floors and parts of the facade bent. KAFD entrances were closed and people evacuated; no casualties were reported initially. Aramco's building in the district was hit on 8 November. Semafor reported KAFD offices had been shut for weeks after an early-October attack on Riyadh airport, and that some expatriates are leaving.
sections.differing: Houthi spokesman Yahya Sarea claimed on 18 November a large cruise-missile attack on King Khalid airport and a Riyadh financial center (via Xinhua/CGTN, state media); the coalition said it intercepted two drones. Reuters said the Houthis made no immediate statement on the PIF strike.
sections.unknown: Missile type, whether the tower was the intended target, casualties, PIF's own statement, and Houthi claim of responsibility remain unconfirmed.

items.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold Shenzhen trilateral and issue four-point 'peace declaration'
items.summary: The US, Chinese and Russian presidents met for about 80 minutes in Shenzhen on the APEC sidelines and issued a four-point declaration on UN reform, refined fuel supply, state immunity and nuclear-risk dialogue. Analysts note little concrete substance.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Declaration text published by Xinhua; Reuters, Al Jazeera, Semafor report meeting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026, Xinhua full text of declaration (18:58 Beijing time, about 10:58 UK); Reuters, Al Jazeera, Semafor same day

sections.happened: On 19 November 2026, Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump met in Shenzhen on the sidelines of APEC, after separate bilateral meetings. Semafor put the trilateral at 80 minutes. Xinhua published a four-point declaration: UN reform, more refined petroleum production and supply with stable energy flows, state-official immunity and limits on the International Criminal Court, and a dialogue on nuclear risks and non-proliferation. Trump called it historic. Al Jazeera reports Iran was not referenced beyond Trump's remarks.
sections.unknown: No timetable or format for the nuclear dialogue is stated, nor how fuel supply will rise. Whether Putin attends the Miami G20 next month is unconfirmed.
sections.differing: Reuters says China and Russia reported the declaration; Xinhua and the Kremlin released it, and none of the leaders commented afterwards. Kremlin said Ukraine was not the central topic. Xi earlier called for banning nuclear weapons; China has resisted arms-control talks. Semafor: long on symbolism, short on substance.

items.headline: Equinor says cyberattack on IT systems is ongoing; production unaffected
items.summary: Equinor detected an ongoing cyberattack on some IT systems on 17 November. By 19 November it was still ongoing; production is normal and no data theft is indicated. No actor has been named; police and security authorities have been informed.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Equinor statements, corroborated by NSM comment and Reuters, NTB reporting.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 17:55 GMT (18:55 CET), Equinor company statement

sections.happened: Equinor, the Norwegian state-controlled energy group, announced on 17 November that it had detected an ongoing cyberattack on certain IT systems. A 19 November update (11:40 CET) said the attack was still ongoing and it was too early to say how long recovery would take. Production is running as normal, and there are no indications that data has been stolen. Equinor said the attack does not appear to be specifically targeting it, and has reported the matter to police. Employees reportedly had trouble accessing applications; Reuters cited a source saying internal email was down.
sections.technical: Equinor said the incident is not a virus attack, so there is no risk of it spreading. It has not disclosed the access vector, the affected systems or an actor, and no IOCs or CVEs have been published. The company said it gained a clearer understanding of how the attack was carried out on 18 November but gave no detail.
sections.guidance: Equinor said it is in continuous contact with national security authorities. Norway's NSM said it was aware and ready to provide support if needed.
sections.differing: Equinor's later statement says the attack does not appear to target it specifically; earlier wording gave no view on targeting. No group has claimed responsibility.
sections.unknown: Attacker, entry method, affected systems, data exposure and restoration time are undisclosed.

items.headline: UK tribunal rejects Home Office secrecy over Apple technical capability notice
items.summary: The Investigatory Powers Tribunal ruled on 19 November that the Home Office had not shown that confirming a technical capability notice served on Apple would harm national security. Lawfulness of the notice is undecided; a substantive hearing is expected in 2027.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Tribunal judgment reported consistently by Computer Weekly, The Record and TechCrunch. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026, Computer Weekly (published 15:41 UK); TechCrunch 15:32 UK (7:32 PST)

sections.happened: Three judges of the Investigatory Powers Tribunal found on 19 November that the Home Office has given Apple a technical capability notice (TCN) and rejected its argument that confirming this would damage national security. Apple, Privacy International and Liberty are challenging the Home Secretary's powers. The tribunal said the government had not applied 'neither confirm nor deny' consistently, citing media briefings by officials and permission for Apple to brief US officials.
sections.unknown: The notice's contents, scope and current form are undisclosed. Lawfulness is undecided. The Home Office has not commented. Which details may be released is for later hearings.
sections.differing: TechCrunch reports the original order was later narrowed to British users' data and that Apple challenged that too; the other outlets do not mention this. The Home Office said it does not comment on operational matters.

items.headline: ICJ finds Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
items.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled on 19 November 2026 in The Gambia v. Myanmar that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, per Al Jazeera by nine of 15 judges, and ordered cessation, prosecutions, restitution and a compensation plan.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Court judgment delivered publicly; reported by Reuters, Al Jazeera, Semafor. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026, about 10:00 CET (09:00 UK), Reuters via Al-Monitor

sections.happened: The International Court of Justice, presided over by Yuji Iwasawa, ruled on Thursday 19 November 2026 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, in the case The Gambia brought in 2019. Al Jazeera reports nine of 15 judges found genocide and the decision is final. It found killings, sexual violence, village destruction and a breach of the duty to prevent genocide. It ordered cessation, prosecutions, restitution and a compensation plan within two years. Reuters called it the first time a state was found responsible for genocide at the court.
sections.unknown: The full judgment text and ICJ press release could not be read. Myanmar's response, the full vote breakdown and any enforcement steps are not yet reported in the sources read.
sections.differing: Semafor says Myanmar insists its 2017 crackdown was a fair response to militia attacks; the court rejected this. Casualty figures vary: Semafor 700,000+ fled, Al Jazeera about 750,000; both cite about 10,000 killed.

items.headline: New US chip export rules hit Southeast Asia shipments and Chinese firms
items.summary: Commerce's BIS interim final rule requires a license for advanced AI chips to data centers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, targeting remote access by China-headquartered firms.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: BIS rule released 16 Nov; confirmed by Gibson Dunn analysis; rule text not fetched. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 16 Nov 2026 (BIS release date); reported 18-19 Nov

sections.happened: On 16 Nov 2026 BIS released an interim final rule, Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors. It adds license requirements for advanced computing items to five countries, and requires overseas data centers serving China-headquartered firms to obtain licenses by mid-February.
sections.technical: The rule extends controls to remote access to compute from controlled chips, tightens presumptions for foundries and packagers, and formally rescinds the AI Diffusion Framework from the EAR. US-headquartered firms are exempt if they report shipments.
sections.guidance: Commerce says it will monitor countries that tolerate evasion and consider import restrictions, new license requirements, export-control status downgrades and sanctions.
sections.differing: CFR's Jessica Brandt says building will be slower and costlier; MBSB's Ming San Soong expects a two-tier Malaysian industry, with sites reliant on Chinese customers hit harder.
sections.unknown: Enforcement against Megaspeed-linked firms, and whether monitoring leads to penalties on named countries, are not established. The rule text itself was not read.

items.headline: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth while returning no science or engineering data
items.summary: NASA calculates Voyager 1 passed one light-day (about 25.9 billion km) from Earth on 18 November. Since 14 November it has sent only a carrier signal, with no science or engineering data; engineers suspect its data-formatting computer.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: NASA published both the milestone and the data fault; independent outlets agree.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026, evening US (NASA Science mission blog, published 20:37 EST)

sections.happened: NASA calculated that Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth at 5:16am EST (10:16 GMT) on 18 November, about 25.9 billion km (16.1 billion miles). The probe launched in 1977 and is the most distant human-made object. On 14 November the mission team found it had stopped sending science and engineering data, although a Deep Space Network antenna at Canberra still locked onto its carrier signal. NASA planned to confirm the milestone on 19 November using the carrier signal and trajectory calculations.
sections.technical: NASA says the carrier signal shows the Attitude and Articulation Control computer is keeping the antenna pointed at Earth and the transmitter works. The missing data suggests a fault in the onboard computer that collects and formats subsystem data. A similar 2023 carrier-only episode was traced to an onboard computer and fixed. Round-trip signal time exceeds 48 hours.
sections.guidance: NASA says diagnosis may take weeks or longer. The team is checking for a link to an October 2026 communications gap of about 48 hours, after which the spacecraft resumed contact by itself.
sections.differing: The Register says the October pause may have involved safe mode after a thruster failover; the NASA text read says only that contact resumed by itself. Cause of either event is unconfirmed.
sections.unknown: The cause of the data loss, whether it connects to the October gap, and whether data can be restored are not yet known.

items.headline: NIH director seeks probe of 2020 COVID origin paper
items.summary: NIH director Jay Bhattacharya has asked Nature Medicine to investigate the authorship of its 2020 'proximal origin' paper on SARS-CoV-2, alleging it was ghostwritten by former NIH officials.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Letter reported by Science from search excerpt; letter text and full article not read. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026 per Science; exact time not shown in the excerpt seen

sections.happened: Jay Bhattacharya, NIH director, wrote an unusual letter to the editor of Nature Medicine requesting an investigation into the authorship of 'The proximal origin of SARS-CoV-2', published 17 March 2020. Science reports the letter asks for a reply within 30 days on any plans for a review.
sections.differing: Ian Lipkin, a named author, rejects the suggestions, saying the final authorship list accurately reflects the scientists who conceived of, drafted and revised the paper. Science notes the letter offers no new evidence to back up the ghostwriting assertion.
sections.unknown: Nature Medicine's response had not been reported. Fauci and Collins declined comment; Andersen and Garry declined to address it. The Science article itself returned HTTP 403.
